original_value: AbstractBackgroundOrthology inference is normally based on full-length protein sequences. However, most proteins contain independently folding and recurring regions, domains. The domain architecture of a protein is vital for its function, and recombination events mean individual domains can have different evolutionary histories. It has previously been shown that orthologous proteins may differ in domain architecture, creating challenges for orthology inference methods operating on full-length sequences. We have developed Domainoid, a new tool aiming to overcome these challenges faced by full-length orthology methods by inferring orthology on the domain level. It employs the InParanoid algorithm on single domains separately, to infer groups of orthologous domains.ResultsThis domain-oriented approach allows detection of discordant domain orthologs, cases where different domains on the same protein have different evolutionary histories. In addition to domain level analysis, protein level orthology based on the fraction of domains that are orthologous can be inferred. Domainoid orthology assignments were compared to those yielded by the conventional full-length approach InParanoid, and were validated in a standard benchmark.ConclusionsOur results show that domain-based orthology inference can reveal many orthologous relationships that are not found by full-length sequence approaches.Availabilityhttps://bitbucket.org/sonnhammergroup/domainoid/

result.paraphrase: AbstractBackgroundOrthology inference is usually carried out using complete protein sequences. Yet most proteins include recurring, independently folding regions called domains. Because domain architecture is crucial to protein function and recombination can give individual domains distinct evolutionary histories, orthologous proteins may differ in their domain composition, which makes full-length orthology methods difficult to apply. To address these problems, we developed Domainoid, a new tool that infers orthology at the domain level rather than from full-length sequences. It uses the InParanoid algorithm separately on individual domains to identify groups of orthologous domains.ResultsThis domain-focused strategy can detect discordant domain orthologs, where different domains within the same protein have different evolutionary histories. Beyond domain-level analysis, it can also infer protein-level orthology from the fraction of domains that are orthologous. Domainoid orthology assignments were compared with those from the conventional full-length InParanoid approach and validated using a standard benchmark.ConclusionsOur results indicate that domain-based orthology inference can uncover many orthologous relationships missed by full-length sequence methods.Availabilityhttps://bitbucket.org/sonnhammergroup/domainoid/
